scope: Build-only validation plus a runtime A/B check of a minimal upstream-shaped staging-reclamation patch for the Vulkan wrapper (leegao/bionic-vulkan-wrapper at source commit 3abf48704a4d9303967a0811c0dc8ff8567d613b). The patch implements the fence-gated staging GC TODO at wrapper_device.c:1674-1675, initializes the staging tracking struct (review C9), checks its allocation (C10), adds failure cleanup to CreateStagingBuffer (C8), and makes the internal staging buffer + memory raw-dispatch objects so the reclamation path does not re-enter wrapper bookkeeping (review O1/C11 class). Patch application and compilation were verified; ELF identity was compared with the recorded candidate build; the patched stripped library was then run on a freshly booted Android emulator (emulator-5556, AVD Vapor_UI_API36, arm64-v8a/API 36, 4 KB pages, llvmpipe Vulkan) with the prior native probe, A/B against the recorded candidate payload. No Vapor app code, driver routing, payload or Gradle/build file was changed, and no game/Steam/Wine process was started.

component.name: vulkan-wrapper staging resources (bionic-vulkan-wrapper)
component.note: The Codex tree was read only. The patch was applied to a fresh extraction of wrapper-build/source.tar.gz in <workspace>/wrapper-staging-reclaim/work/source.

hunks.purpose: Add wrapper_command_buffer::usage_flags so one-time-submit command buffers can be distinguished from re-submittable ones.
C9/C10: allocate wrapper_staging_resources with vk_zalloc, zero initialise ready/use_vk_object, and log-instead-of-crash on allocation failure.
Fix the unhandled-type WLOGE format call (missing argument) found while re-reading the free path.

Add set_staging_resources_fence() and reclaim_completed_staging_resources(); stamp the application submission fence onto one-time-submit staging resources after successful vkQueueSubmit/vkQueueSubmit2; reclaim in vkWaitForFences and vkDeviceWaitIdle; reclaim a command buffer's staging resources in vkBeginCommandBuffer and vkResetCommandBuffer.
Create the internal staging VkBuffer through the raw dispatch table (CHECK instead of WCHECK), with a comment explaining why wrapper bookkeeping is deliberately bypassed.
C8: raw AllocateMemory/BindBufferMemory for the staging memory, plus destroy-buffer on allocate failure and destroy-buffer + free-memory on bind failure.
Image-view staging path: track the temporary VkImageView on the recording command buffer instead of the image.
Buffer path: replace the TODO with command-buffer ownership and track the staging VkBuffer/VkDeviceMemory on the recording command buffer.

apply_verification.method: Fresh copy of the three pristine base files in /tmp/applytest/src/vulkan/wrapper, then patch(1) from the tree root.

semantics.problem_addressed: The prior review found that per-image BCn staging VkBuffer/VkDeviceMemory (and the image-view path's VkImageView) are tracked on wimg->staging_resources, that wrapper_staging_resources::ready is never assigned, that the fence branch in free_staging_resources_if_ready is dead because its only caller passes cleanup_everything=true, and that the intended queue-fence GC is the TODO at wrapper_device.c:1674-1675. Long-lived images therefore accumulate two resources (or one view) per upload until image/device destroy.
semantics.ownership_change: Staging resources are now owned by the wrapper_command_buffer that records the commands referencing them (both the VkBuffer/VkDeviceMemory path and the image-view path), not by the image. The image's staging_resources list is still initialized and its destroy path still calls free_staging_resources_final, but it is now empty in both paths.
completion_gated_reclaim_points: vkBeginCommandBuffer / vkResetCommandBuffer: Vulkan only allows these from the initial state, which requires a preceding reset, and a command buffer can only be reset once all submissions using it have completed. The command buffer's staging list is therefore freed unconditionally at these points (free_staging_resources_final / cleanup_everything=true). This is the reclaim path for re-submittable command buffers.

vkWaitForFences: after a VK_SUCCESS wait, one-time-submit command buffers whose staging resources were stamped with one of the waited fences are released via free_staging_resources_if_ready(..., cleanup_everything=false), which is the fence branch that was dead before this patch. One-time-submit command buffers can never be resubmitted, so releasing as soon as that submission's fence has signalled is safe even though the command buffer itself may still exist.

vkDeviceWaitIdle: after VK_SUCCESS all submitted work is complete, so one-time-submit command buffers that were handed a submission fence are released unconditionally (cleanup_everything=true) without dereferencing the fence, which may already have been destroyed by the application. This covers applications that submit with a fence but wait with vkDeviceWaitIdle.
wrapper_command_buffer_destroy (existing): still frees the command buffer's staging list with cleanup_everything=true on vkFreeCommandBuffers/vkDestroyCommandPool/vkDestroyDevice.
semantics.fence_assignment: WRAPPER_QueueSubmit and WRAPPER_QueueSubmit2, after a successful submit, walk the submitted command buffers and set wrapper_staging_resources::ready to the VkFence the application passed, but only for command buffers recorded with VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_USAGE_ONE_TIME_SUBMIT_BIT. Re-submittable command buffers are deliberately not handed to the fence because a later submission would reuse the same recorded staging handles; their resources are released from the begin/reset/destroy paths instead. Submission fences are only stored; no wrapper-owned fence or extra submit is created. Queue-submit wait/signal semaphores are not tracked.
safety_notes: The stored fence handle is dereferenced only inside WRAPPER_WaitForFences after that call returned VK_SUCCESS, i.e. while the application's own wait call is still on the stack and the fence is valid; the device-idle path uses cleanup_everything=true and never touches the handle.
For waitAll=VK_FALSE with more than one fence the signalled fence is not knowable; such resources are left for the device-idle or command-buffer-destroy path rather than guessed.
A one-time-submit command buffer submitted without a fence keeps its resources until begin/reset/destroy; those paths are still completion-gated by Vulkan valid usage.
Free order is unchanged (list insertion order: VkBuffer before its VkDeviceMemory; forward iteration).

review_findings_addressed.C1/C3: Fence-gated/command-buffer-gated reclamation replaces destroy-only retention; growth is now bounded by command-buffer lifetime instead of image lifetime (and by submission-fence completion for one-time submits). Runtime growth reduction is NOT measured.
review_findings_addressed.C8: CreateStagingBuffer failure paths now destroy the buffer / free the memory.
review_findings_addressed.C9: wrapper_staging_resources::ready and use_vk_object are zero-initialised via vk_zalloc.
review_findings_addressed.C10: add_staging_resource_to no longer dereferences an unchecked vk_alloc result; it logs and returns.
review_findings_addressed.O1/C11 class: The internal staging VkBuffer and VkDeviceMemory are now created and freed with the raw dispatch table only (CHECK/CHECKV), so they are never registered in device->buffer_map and never enter the wrapper emulated VkDeviceMemory path; raw FreeMemory is balanced in both the memoryMapPlaced-emulated and non-emulated cases. This also avoids re-entering WRAPPER_DestroyBuffer/WRAPPER_FreeMemory while device->resource_mutex is held by command-buffer teardown (which would deadlock). The O1 double-free is therefore not reachable through staging allocations after this patch, but this was not runtime-validated.

confirmed: tools/vulkan-wrapper/staging-reclaim.patch applies to a pristine extraction of source commit 3abf48704a4d9303967a0811c0dc8ff8567d613b with `patch -p1 --fuzz=0` (forward dry-run, forward apply, reverse dry-run all clean); applied file hashes equal the files used for the build.

The patched tree compiles and links the full aarch64 Android wrapper library with the recorded Meson/NDK recipe (meson 1.9.1, NDK r27.3.13750724 clang 18.0.4, record link flags, 16 KB max-page-size): ninja reached 471/471 and produced libvulkan_wrapper.so. No compiler warnings or errors were emitted for wrapper_device.c or wrapper_objects.c.

The patch's intended sources are the only changed files: wrapper_objects.h (usage_flags field), wrapper_objects.c (zalloc + null check + init, WLOGE format fix), wrapper_device.c (new fence/command-buffer reclaim helpers and vkQueueSubmit/vkQueueSubmit2/vkWaitForFences/vkDeviceWaitIdle/vkBeginCommandBuffer/vkResetCommandBuffer hooks, staging allocation/failure cleanup and raw internal allocation, tracking-parent changes at both staging sites).

The new completion/reclaim hooks are present in the linked binary as local hidden symbols: wrapper_BeginCommandBuffer, wrapper_ResetCommandBuffer, wrapper_WaitForFences, wrapper_DeviceWaitIdle, wrapper_QueueSubmit, wrapper_QueueSubmit2, plus reclaim_completed_staging_resources; wrapper_image_destroy and wrapper_command_buffer_destroy sizes are unchanged, so no existing destroy logic was edited.

The built library matches the recorded candidate ELF identity for the compared properties: SONAME libvulkan_wrapper.so, the same 20 NEEDED libraries, four LOAD segments all aligned 0x4000, 4073 exported symbols whose full [Type, Bind, Vis, Name] set is identical to the recorded candidate-exports.json, and an identical undefined-symbol name list.
No existing Vapor repository file was modified and nothing was committed; the only repository additions are tools/vulkan-wrapper/staging-reclaim.patch and this receipt.

Runtime validation on emulator-5556 (AVD Vapor_UI_API36, arm64-v8a/API 36, 4 KB pages) with the prior native probe: 7 runs, all exit code 0, all pixel checks passed, 'PASS clean-exit' in every run, no wrapper staging-path errors and no probe crash/tombstone.

A/B against the recorded candidate on the same emulator/probe: control (candidate.so, USE_IMAGE_VIEW=0, 32 cycles) releases 64 staging resources in a single call at vkDestroyImage; the patched library releases the same 64 resources as 32 two-resource calls during the workload (command-buffer free), and USE_IMAGE_VIEW=1 releases 32 tracked image views as 32 one-resource calls.

Fence-gated reclamation is runtime-validated: one-time-submit command buffers with an application fence release their staging resources inside vkWaitForFences (release log lines appear between the probe's before-wait/after-wait markers), and the same resources are released inside vkDeviceWaitIdle when the application never waits the fence.

Command-buffer ownership is runtime-validated for re-submittable command buffers: even when the application passes a fence, staging resources are released inside vkFreeCommandBuffers (between after-wait and after-free-cmd markers), matching the design that such command buffers must not be handed to the submission fence.
not_validated: vkBeginCommandBuffer/vkResetCommandBuffer reclaim and command-buffer re-record/reuse cycles were not exercised in a dedicated run (early releases observed came from vkFreeCommandBuffers, vkWaitForFences and vkDeviceWaitIdle).

The wrapper-emulated-memory / VK_EXT_map_memory_placed path was not exercised on the emulator (lavapipe does not enable it); the raw-dispatch staging allocation change and the O1 double-free fix are not runtime-proven.
Concurrency/thread-safety is not validated: staging lists are still mutated without the per-object resource_mutex and the wrapper still relies on Vulkan external synchronization.
No Khronos validation-layer run was performed, so no VUID cleanliness is claimed for the new hooks or the changed staging ownership.
No real game/streaming workload or physical phone was used, so the retention/memory-growth reduction is not quantified (only the release points are shown).
Only binary fences are handled; submit-time semaphores/timeline semaphores are not tracked.
vkQueueSubmit2 is compiled and symbol-checked but was not executed (the probe uses vkQueueSubmit).
Only 4 KB pages were used at runtime; the 16 KB-page case was not re-validated with this patch.
A one-time-submit command buffer submitted without a fence was not exercised; expected bounded retention until begin/reset/destroy is unverified.
residual_risks_not_addressed: free_staging_resources_if_ready still ignores driver return codes (review C12) and still destroys objects through the raw dispatch table; wrapper bookkeeping for staging is avoided by construction but not asserted.

A one-time-submit command buffer submitted without a fence, or submitted with a fence the application never waits (and never calls vkDeviceWaitIdle for), keeps its staging resources until the command buffer is re-begun/reset/freed. This is bounded retention, not a leak past command-buffer destruction.

The image destroy path still calls free_staging_resources_final on wimg->staging_resources, but the image lists are now always empty. Keeping the call is deliberate to preserve the existing failure-path behavior if another tracking site is added later.

Staging views tracked on a command buffer can outlive a destroyed parent image if the application destroys the image while the command buffer still holds recorded references; this is an application valid-usage violation and the wrapper still does not detect or prevent it (prior review C2).

The patch does not move the reclamation into queue-submit itself for re-submittable command buffers; that is intentional because the application's fence cannot prove the command buffer will not be resubmitted.

comparison.patched_image_view_path: 32 'Tracking stagingImageView' -> 32 x 'Released 1 staging resources' per cycle; 32/32 views accounted for before destroy.
comparison.one_time_submit_fence: 8 tracking -> 8 x 'Released 2' calls between 'MARKER before-wait' and 'MARKER after-wait', i.e. inside vkWaitForFences via the previously dead fence branch. Confirms the submission-fence readiness assignment and the fence-gated reclaim.
comparison.one_time_submit_device_idle: 8 tracking -> 8 x 'Released 2' between 'MARKER before-device-idle' and 'MARKER after-device-idle', i.e. inside vkDeviceWaitIdle. The probe deliberately never waited the submission fence, so the device-idle reclaim path is validated and does not require a live/destroyable fence handle.
comparison.resubmittable_command_buffer_with_fence: 8 tracking -> 8 x 'Released 2' between 'MARKER after-wait' and 'MARKER after-free-cmd', i.e. inside vkFreeCommandBuffers. Confirms the design decision that re-submittable command buffers are NOT handed to the submission fence and instead release at command-buffer destruction.
comparison.image_view_plus_one_time_submit_fence: 8 views -> 8 x 'Released 1' inside vkWaitForFences; the image-view path also releases early.
comparison.arithmetic: r0: 32x2=64 released in 1 call; r1: 32x2=64 in 32 calls; r2: 32x1=32 in 32 calls; r3/r4/r5: 8x2=16 in 8 calls; r6: 8x1=8 in 8 calls. Tracked minus released = 0 in every patched run.
comparison.timing: the patched workload releases happen while rendering continues (either per submission or per command buffer), whereas the control holds all 64 resources until image destroy; this is the unbounded-growth behavior the patch targets.

what_is_now_validated: The patch's reclamation actually happens at runtime: per-submission-fence (one-time-submit CBs), per-vkDeviceWaitIdle (one-time-submit CBs submitted with a fence the app never waited), and per-command-buffer-free (re-submittable CBs) instead of only at vkDestroyImage.
The previously dead fence branch in free_staging_resources_if_ready is now exercised and releases the expected resources only when the waited fence has signalled.
The image-view staging path (default USE_IMAGE_VIEW=1) tracks and releases its temporary VkImageView(s) early, and the buffer path releases VkBuffer+VkDeviceMemory pairs early.

The A/B difference against the recorded candidate is exactly the intended behavior change: control releases 64 resources in one call at image destroy; patched releases 64 resources across 32 calls during the workload (and 32 image views across 32 calls in view mode).
No error or crash was observed in the probe: all runs exited 0, all pixel checks passed, no wrapper staging-path errors, no probe crashes/tombstones.
what_is_still_pending: The vkBeginCommandBuffer / vkResetCommandBuffer reclaim path was not isolated in a dedicated run; the observed early releases came from vkFreeCommandBuffers, vkWaitForFences and vkDeviceWaitIdle. A run that resets a long-lived command buffer (or vkResetCommandPool) and re-begins it is still needed.

The conditional double-free risk on the wrapper-emulated-memory path (VK_EXT_map_memory_placed + VkPhysicalDeviceMapMemoryPlacedFeaturesEXT.memoryMapPlaced) was not exercised; the emulator lavapipe does not enable it. The raw-dispatch staging allocation change removed staging from that path by construction, but this is not runtime-proven.
Concurrency/thread-safety (multi-threaded recording + destroys) was not tested.
Khronos validation layers were not enabled, so no VUID cleanliness is claimed for the new hooks or the changed ownership.
No real game/streaming workload or physical phone was used; memory growth reduction was not measured (only the release-point change is shown).
Submit-time semaphores/timeline semaphores are not tracked, and vkQueueSubmit2 (only vkQueueSubmit was used by the probe) was not executed.
PAGE_SIZE on this run was 4096; the 16 KB-page behavior was not re-validated with this patch.
A one-time-submit command buffer submitted without any fence was not exercised (it is expected to retain resources until begin/reset/destroy).
